You are matching code-review findings against a known bug. Reply with ONLY a JSON object.

KNOWN BUG: When the target is itself a shadow host, its own shadow content is hidden.

Rules:
- Answer "yes" only if the text describes THIS specific bug: the same faulty behaviour in the same situation. A finding about a nearby but different behaviour (another header, another edge case, a different race) is "no".
- A finding that says the behaviour was checked and PASSED, or that the code handles it correctly, is "no".
- Wording does not matter; the behaviour does.
- For handoffs: count only text that tells the implementor to fix this bug (a reported finding, a fix instruction). Restated acceptance criteria that merely describe the desired behaviour do NOT count as carrying the finding unless the handoff ties them to a reported failure.

=== REVIEW 1 FINDINGS ===
- [blocking] `root` is ignored for shadow roots. `getTargetShadowRoots` ignores `options.root`, and `observe()` attaches the observer to every target shadow root in full. Nodes appended outside `root` are then hidden. Reproduced with `{root: container}` where `container` is inside shadow root S: appending a `button` to S outside `container` gave `expect(added).not.toHaveAttribute('aria-hidden')` → `Received: aria-hidden="true"`. The same happens with a light-DOM root that does not contain the host chain (P7). Light DOM does not do this (`LIGHT outsideRoot null added null` in my reference run). The probe passes when the root is `document.body`.
- [minor] Inconsistent state with `root` inside a shadow root: a sibling in S outside `root` is not hidden at call time, but the same sibling appended after the call is hidden.
- [minor] A target moved into a shadow root of a host added after the call (`r2.appendChild(t)`, host `h2` aria-hidden) stays visible in the DOM but sits under an aria-hidden host, which hides it from AT. The shadow root of `h2` is not observed. Light DOM behaves the same way, so this is parity.
- [minor] `shouldUseInert` on shadow content is not reproduced. jsdom has no `inert` on HTMLElement, so `supportsInert` is false and every probe ran the aria-hidden path. Inert needs a real browser to check.
- [minor] The `root` option has no test in the new describe block, which is how the bug above got through.
=== IMPLEMENTOR HANDOFF 1 (sent after review 1) ===
Repo /tmp/ff-eval-8c0hlz_5/workspace. Fix round on an uncommitted change (see `git diff packages/@react-aria/overlays`) that makes `ariaHideOutside` in packages/@react-aria/overlays/src/ariaHideOutside.ts shadow DOM aware under `shadowDOM()`.

GOAL: Respect the `root` option inside shadow roots. Reviewer reproduced a blocking bug: `getTargetShadowRoots(targets)` adds every shadow root on a target's chain and the observer watches each in full, so with `{root: el}` where `el` is inside shadow root S (target inside el), appending a node to S outside `el` gets aria-hidden. The same thing happens with a light-DOM root that doesn't contain the host chain. In the light DOM, nothing above root is ever hidden.
Fix: only collect a shadow root if its host is inside `root` (`nodeContains(root, shadowRoot.host)`; pass `root` into getTargetShadowRoots). That also stops walking and observing the roots above `root`. Keep everything else unchanged.

FILES: packages/@react-aria/overlays/src/ariaHideOutside.ts; tests at the END of the existing `describe` for shadow DOM at the bottom of packages/@react-aria/overlays/test/ariaHideOutside.test.js (reuse its helpers, e.g. appendShadowHost).
CONSTRAINTS: Don't modify pre-existing tests or other packages.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- AC1 With `enableShadowDOM()` on, `ariaHideOutside([target])` where target is inside a shadow root hides (aria-hidden, or inert when shouldUseInert) every sibling element of the target's ancestors inside that shadow root, every sibling of the host in the enclosing root(s) up to the document/root option, and nothing on the path: the target, its ancestors inside the shadow root, and every host on the chain stay unhidden.
- AC2 Content added after the call anywhere inside a target's shadow root or any enclosing shadow root (outside targets) gets hidden; content added inside a target stays visible. Elements with `data-live-announcer="true"` or `data-react-aria-top-layer="true"`, whether already inside those shadow roots or added to them later, stay visible, as in the light DOM.
- AC3 Targets in different shadow roots both stay visible, with both hosts visible and all other siblings in both shadow roots and body hidden; added content in either root is hidden.
- AC4 The returned function removes every aria-hidden/inert it added and stops observing; nested/stacked calls work with shadow targets.
- AC5 With shadow DOM support off, behavior is unchanged.
- AC6 Unrelated shadow hosts are hidden as a single element; slotted targets aren't hidden via shadow-internal wrappers.
- AC7 Tests in ariaHideOutside.test.js at the end; `yarn jest packages/@react-aria/overlays`, `yarn eslint`, `yarn check-types` pass.
- AC8 Nothing above or outside the `root` option is hidden, at call time or later, including inside shadow roots. Tests: (a) root element inside shadow root S: siblings in S outside root are not hidden at call time, and nodes appended to S outside root later are not hidden either, while nodes appended inside root outside the target are; (b) a light-DOM root that doesn't contain the host: content appended into S is not hidden.

CHECKS: while working `yarn jest packages/@react-aria/overlays/test/ariaHideOutside.test.js`; at the end `yarn jest packages/@react-aria/overlays`, `yarn eslint packages/@react-aria/overlays`, `yarn check-types`.
